summary:
SPACECARE – Smart Diabetes Monitoring & Emergency System for Astronauts

SPACECARE is a smart medical system designed to monitor diabetes and protect astronauts during space missions, with the potential to support diabetic patients on Earth.

The project combines a smart medical watch, a mobile application, artificial intelligence, and an emergency response system. The watch monitors glucose levels through an approved Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) sensor, alongside vital signs such as heart rate, blood oxygen, skin temperature, and physical activity.

Artificial intelligence analyzes the collected data, detects abnormal glucose changes, and estimates the risk of severe low or high blood sugar, providing early warnings when needed.

The mobile application provides dedicated interfaces for patients, doctors, caregivers, and emergency teams. It also generates health reports and includes an intelligent medical chatbot that offers guidance based on approved medical protocols.

One of the system's key features is its ability to store data and maintain essential alerts even without an internet connection, making it suitable for space environments.

SPACECARE aims to provide smarter diabetes monitoring, early warnings, and faster emergency response, both in space and on Earth.
details: SPACECARE – Project Questions & Answers 1. What is its function and how does it work? SPACECARE is a smart medical watch designed to monitor diabetes, especially in astronauts. It uses an approved CGM sensor to track glucose levels and monitors heart rate, oxygen, skin temperature, and activity. AI analyzes the data, estimates health risks, and sends early alerts through a connected mobile application. 2. What are its benefits? - Continuous health monitoring. - Early detection of dangerous glucose changes. - Automatic medical reports. - Faster emergency response. - Remote medical supervision. - Offline data storage and essential alerts. 3. What is its expected impact? SPACECARE aims to improve astronauts' safety during space missions. It can also help diabetic patients on Earth, especially elderly people, through early warnings and faster medical support. 4. What tools and technologies are proposed? - Hardware: ESP32. - Sensors: CGM, PPG, SpO2, temperature, and motion sensors. - Programming: Python and Flutter. - Backend: FastAPI. - Database: PostgreSQL. - AI: Risk prediction models. - Connectivity: Bluetooth and wireless communication. 5. What is the creative aspect of the project? It combines a smart watch, AI health analysis, medical communication, and emergency response in one system designed for space environments, including limited internet connectivity. 6. What factors did the team consider? Astronaut safety, microgravity, device size and weight, battery life, sensor accuracy, internet limitations, data privacy, comfort, false alarms, and testing under simulated space conditions.
